title: USF Vocabulary Catalogue
purpose: Defines the controlled values (canonical identifiers, historical aliases, and forbidden tokens) that future USF schemas, registries, validators, ADRs, evidence envelopes, source-import maps, and AI agents MUST use. It answers what exact values are allowed for governed fields and classifications. It does NOT define concepts (ontology), classification systems (taxonomy), shapes (schemas), or instance indexes (registries).
normativeLanguage: Requirement words (MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, MAY) follow BCP 14 as defined in docs/architecture/standards-profile.md section 6. Only uppercase forms are normative.
scopeNote: This artefact is a vocabulary, not an ontology, taxonomy, schema, or registry. It enumerates controlled values; it does not define concepts, classify them, validate shapes, or index instances.

governance.valueSetStatusMeaning: A value set with status 'active' is the canonical controlled set in force for reference and authoring NOW; it does not assert that a validator yet enforces it. rules: Vocabulary belongs to USF semantic definitions and provides exact allowed values for fields and classifications.
Vocabulary MUST align with the ontology and the taxonomy catalogue.
Vocabulary MUST NOT create new concepts outside the ontology without recording deferred work.
Vocabulary MUST NOT create new classifications outside the taxonomy without recording deferred work.
Vocabulary changes can alter semantic meaning and MAY require ADR review.
Vocabulary removals MUST include a disposition.
Vocabulary renames MUST preserve aliases and lineage.
Vocabulary values MUST use stable semantic names.
Vocabulary values MUST NOT use migration-phase names.
../react names MAY appear as historical aliases or source references, not as future canonical values unless semantically justified.
Future AI agents MUST use vocabulary values where available instead of inventing free text.
governance.aliasConvention: Aliases are recorded in each value set's 'aliases' array as objects mapping an alias id to a canonical value id, with a sourceNote. Aliases are not listed again in the 'values' array. An alias MUST resolve to a canonical value present in the same set.

vocabularyDesignPrinciples: Prefer semantic names over source-path names.
Prefer canonical values that survive implementation changes.
Preserve historical source names as aliases, not canonical future values.
Distinguish active values from deprecated or forbidden values.
Distinguish exact allowed values from taxonomy categories.
Avoid over-specific values that encode implementation detail.
Avoid values that encode migration phase.
Treat provider mode and environment as separate dimensions.
Treat proof level and readiness status as separate dimensions.
Treat source evidence and future authority as separate dimensions.
Treat generated reports as lower-authority artefacts.
Include AI guidance for every high-risk value set.
Forbidden: no canonical value may use v2, legacy, old, new, temp, transitional, or redundant usf; historical terms may appear only in aliases or source notes where necessary.
vocabularyRules: Every value set MUST have an id, title, description, status, governed taxonomy references, governed ontology concepts, expected schema consumers, and AI guidance.
Every value MUST have an id, label, description, lifecycle state, and meaning.
Every value MUST identify whether it is canonical, alias, deprecated, forbidden, provisional, or deferred (via its lifecycle field; aliases live in the set's aliases array).
Every alias MUST point to a canonical value in the same set.
Deprecated values MUST include a replacement where possible.
Values MUST be unique within a value set.
Value set IDs MUST be unique.
Value IDs MUST NOT be inferred from ../react paths.
Generated reports MUST NOT introduce new canonical values.
Future schemas MUST reference value sets rather than duplicate enums independently.
